About

A considered approach
to each project.

My work sits between an idea for a place and the decisions needed to develop it. That can mean understanding a market, shaping a concept, reviewing a design or working through the requirements of a hotel brand and operator.

Across hotels, branded residences, leisure attractions and destinations, I have worked alongside the teams responsible for research, design, construction and operations. Those experiences have taught me to look at a project from several perspectives, and to pay attention to how decisions made early on affect what comes later.

I value clear briefs, careful research and open discussion. I try to make complex questions easier to work through, while keeping sight of the people who will eventually visit, stay and work there.

How I can help

A little more clarity,
where a project needs it.

I welcome conversations about research, product development and project reviews. The scope can be a defined question, an early-stage brief or support through a particular phase of development.

01 / UNDERSTAND

Research & direction

Market and destination research, comparable projects and positioning studies to help frame a development opportunity.

Possible outputs: a research note, options assessment or positioning brief.

02 / SHAPE

Concept & product

Concept development, guest journeys, facilities programmes and development briefs that connect the intended experience with project requirements.

Possible outputs: a concept brief, facilities programme or experience framework.

03 / REVIEW

Project & design review

Reviewing proposals, design and brand or operator options against the project's objectives, with attention to guest experience and operational needs.

Possible outputs: a review matrix, comparison of options or recommendations for the next stage.

Working together

Begin with the question.

Every project arrives with its own context. Before suggesting a direction, I would like to understand the decision you are facing, what has already been explored and where another perspective might be useful.

  1. Understand the brief. Agree the question, scope and information available.
  2. Study the context. Examine relevant research, comparable projects and the practical constraints.
  3. Discuss the options. Test assumptions and work through the trade-offs.
  4. Set out the next steps. Bring the findings together in a form the project team can use.

The work may be a short review or a more involved assignment. We can define the scope, timing and deliverables after an initial conversation.

A few practical questions

Before getting in touch.

Does a project need to be fully defined?

No. An early question or outline is a useful starting point. We can first explore what needs to be understood and whether my experience is relevant.

What would be helpful to share?

A short description of the project, its location, current stage, the decision you need support with and any timing considerations. There is no need to send confidential material in the first message.

How is the scope agreed?

After an initial discussion, we can set out the scope, deliverables, timing and fee before any assignment begins.
